file_insights.purpose: Django views for inventory count management operations
key_components: inventory_count_list - Paginated list view with filtering and statistics
inventory_count_detail - Detailed view with variance calculations
inventory_count_create - POST endpoint for creating new counts
inventory_count_start - Initializes count with stock items
inventory_count_save_items - Saves counted quantities via JSON
inventory_count_generate_adjustments - Creates stock movements for variances

patterns_discovered.description: Count follows PLANNED → IN_PROGRESS → COMPLETED → (can generate adjustments) workflow with status validation at each step
Extensive use of select_related() and prefetch_related() to minimize database queries in list and detail views
inventory_count_save_items uses json.loads(request.body) for batch item updates rather than form data
Uses Decimal type for all quantity calculations to avoid floating-point precision issues
All create/update operations track created_by and updated_by users
Each POST endpoint validates preconditions before attempting operations
Automatic stock movement generation based on difference between system_quantity and counted_quantity

gotchas_discovered.description: Prevents same person from being both counter and supervisor, but validation only occurs in create view, not in subsequent updates
inventory_count_start rejects counts if warehouse has no stock with current_quantity > 0, preventing counts of zero-stock locations
Complete operation fails if any item has counted_quantity=NULL, even if intentional (e.g., items to be ignored)
generate_adjustments uses item.counted_quantity as final quantity, but StockMovement model may interpret this differently depending on movement_type handling
json import is inside inventory_count_save_items function instead of module-level, breaking convention
No locking mechanism prevents concurrent edits to same count between checking status and updating items

approach_outcome.description: Create count_views.py with inventory count-related views
approach_outcome.notes: Successfully implemented complete workflow for inventory counting including creation, item population, counting, completion, and automatic adjustment generation. Uses Django best practices with proper query optimization and error handling.

recommendations.recommendation: Add database transaction wrapping around inventory_count_start to ensure atomicity when creating multiple InventoryCountItem records
Verify StockMovement model's handling of ADJUSTMENT type with quantity parameter - confirm it correctly applies the adjustment vs. incrementing
Move json import to module-level imports at top of file for consistency
Add ability to mark items as 'not counted' or 'not found' explicitly rather than leaving NULL, allowing completion with intentionally uncounted items
Add counter-supervisor validation to count update operations, not just creation
Add docstring examples showing expected JSON format for inventory_count_save_items requests
Add logging to adjustment generation to track which items triggered variances for audit purposes
